notes.summary: This topic covers four small question kinds: putting words in dictionary order, putting words in a logical order, word formation from given letters, and the alphabet test (working with letter positions inside a word). SSC asks about 1 question in Tier 1. Each one is quick if you work letter by letter on paper.

concepts.title: Dictionary order: the rules
concepts.body:
1. Compare the first letters. The word with the earlier letter comes first.
  2. If the first letters are the same, compare the second letters, then the third, and so on, until the letters differ.
  3. If one word is the start of the other (Real, Realism), the shorter word comes first.
  4. Capital letters, spaces and hyphens do not change the order in these questions.
PairFirst differenceComes first
Brake / Breada vs e (3rd letter)Brake
Peck / Pebblec vs b (3rd letter)Pebble
Realism / Realisticm vs t (7th letter)Realism
Hatch / HatchbackHatch is the start of HatchbackHatch

concepts.title: Dictionary order: a worked set
concepts.body:
Arrange: 1. Disaster 2. Disappointment 3. Discharge 4. Disappear 5. Disadvantage 6. Disarticulate
  1. All start with "Dis". The 4th letters: a, a, c, a, a, a. So Discharge (c) comes last.
  2. Among the "Disa…" words, look at the 5th letter: s (Disaster), p (Disappointment), p (Disappear), d (Disadvantage), r (Disarticulate). Order: d, p, p, r, s.
  3. Disappear and Disappointment share "Disapp"; then e comes before o, so Disappear first.
Order: Disadvantage, Disappear, Disappointment, Disarticulate, Disaster, Discharge, which is 5, 4, 2, 6, 1, 3.
Tip: group words by their first different letter, then sort within each group.

concepts.title: Logical order
concepts.body:
Here meaning decides the order, not the alphabet. Look for one of these chains:
Kind of chainExample
Life cycleChild, Youth, Adult, Old age
Small to largeCity, State, Country, Continent, World
ProcessCotton, Thread, Fabric, Shirt piece, Shirt
Work stepsConceptualize, Design, Develop, Test, Implement
CareerEducation, Degree, Interview, Job, Retirement
Growth of a plantSeed, Plant, Flower, Fruit
Day partsDawn, Morning, Noon, Evening, Night
Find the clear first and last word, then fill the middle. The options usually differ in one or two places, so check only those.

concepts.title: Word formation
concepts.body:
Can a word be made from the letters of a given word? Each letter can be used only as many times as it appears.
  1. Write the letters of the given word with their counts.
  2. Cross off the letters of the option word one by one.
  3. If a letter is missing, or needed more times than available, the word cannot be formed.
Example: EXAMINATION has E, X, A×2, M, I×2, N×2, T, O. MOTION needs O twice, but there is only one O. So MOTION cannot be formed. NATION, ANIMATE? ANIMATE needs E, A×2, N, I, M, T: all present, so it can be formed.

concepts.title: Counting meaningful words and jumbled letters
concepts.body:
• "How many meaningful words can be formed from the 2nd, 4th, 5th and 6th letters of HOCKEY?" Pick the letters carefully (O, K, E, Y). Then try common words: YOKE. Only one standard English word uses all four, so the answer is one. If no word is possible, the answer is "none".
  • Jumbled letters: AVSEBORINTO rearranges to OBSERVATION. Questions then ask for the position of a letter in that word (R is 5th from the left).
Count the letters of your word against the given letters to be sure nothing is left over.

concepts.title: Number-coded words
concepts.body:
Each letter gets a number, for example E = 1, N = 2, T = 3, S = 4, T = 5, D = 6, U = 7. The letters together spell a word (here STUDENT). Write the word, then its numbers: S = 4, T = 3 or 5, U = 7, D = 6, E = 1, N = 2, T = 5 or 3. Pick the option that matches, remembering a repeated letter can take either of its numbers.
Quick start: find which word the letters make before reading the options.

concepts.title: Alphabet test
concepts.body:
These questions arrange the letters of a word in alphabetical order, or count letters in the alphabet.
  • Letters that stay in place: JEALOUS in alphabetical order is AEJLOSU. Compare place by place: J/A, E/E, A/J, L/L, O/O, U/S, S/U. E, L and O stay in place, so 3.
  • Letters between two letters: after arranging KEYBOARD as ABDEKORY, the third from the right is O and the second from the right is R. Between O and R in the alphabet are P and Q, so 2.
  • Middle letter: the letter midway between H (8) and P (16) is position 12 = L.
Always write the new arrangement under the original word; never compare in your head.

varieties.name: Dictionary order
varieties.how: Compare words letter by letter until they differ. If one word is the start of another, the shorter one comes first.

example.q: Arrange in dictionary order: 1. Realistic 2. Realism 3. Restore 4. Research 5. Resurge
steps: "Real…" words come before "Res…" words because a comes before s.
Realism before Realistic: m comes before t.
Research, Restore, Resurge: the 4th letters are e, t, u.

varieties.name: Logical order
varieties.how: Find what kind of chain the words form (size, process, life stages). Fix the first and last words, then fill the middle.

example.q: Arrange in a logical order: 1. Shirt piece 2. Thread 3. Fabric 4. Shirt 5. Cotton
steps: It is a process: raw cotton becomes a finished shirt.
Cotton → Thread → Fabric → Shirt piece → Shirt.

varieties.name: Word formation
varieties.how: List the letters of the given word with their counts. For each option, cross letters off. A word that needs a missing letter, or a letter more times than available, cannot be formed.

example.q: Which word cannot be formed from EXAMINATION? NATION, ANIMATE, MOTION, TAXI
steps: NATION, ANIMATE and TAXI use only available letters.

varieties.name: Number-coded word
varieties.how: Work out the meaningful word from the letters first. Then write each letter's number in that order and match it with the options.

example.q: E = 1, N = 2, T = 3, S = 4, T = 5, D = 6, U = 7. Which arrangement forms a meaningful word? (a) 4 3 7 6 1 2 5 (b) 4 7 3 6 1 2 5 (c) 6 7 4 3 1 2 5 (d) 4 3 7 1 6 2 5
steps: The letters S, T, U, D, E, N, T make STUDENT.

varieties.name: Alphabet test
varieties.how: Write the letters in alphabetical order under the original word and compare place by place. For "between" questions, use letter positions.

example.q: If the letters of MEADOW are arranged in alphabetical order, how many letters stay in the same place?
steps: Alphabetical order: A D E M O W.
Compare with M E A D O W: M/A, E/D, A/E, D/M, O/O, W/W.
O and W stay in place.

tips: In dictionary order, group words by their first different letter before sorting.
A word that is the start of a longer word always comes first (Hatch before Hatchback).
In word formation, count repeated letters; most wrong options need one extra letter.
For logical order, fix the first and last items, then check only the places where options differ.
In alphabet tests, write the sorted letters under the original word.
EJOTY (E = 5, J = 10, O = 15, T = 20, Y = 25) speeds up midway and counting questions.
traps: Stopping at the first letter when words share a long prefix (Disappear and Disappointment differ only at the 7th letter).
Using a letter twice in word formation when it appears only once.
Counting the end letters themselves in "how many letters between" questions. Between O and R are only P and Q.
Treating logical order like dictionary order.

questions.q:
Select the correct sequence of the following words as they would appear in an English dictionary.
1. Bread 2. Bring 3. Brake 4. Breath
questions.solution:
All start with "Br". Third letters: Bread (e), Bring (i), Brake (a), Breath (e).
Brake (a) comes first, Bring (i) last.
Bread vs Breath: "Brea-d" vs "Brea-t" → d before t, so Bread then Breath.
Order: Brake, Bread, Breath, Bring = 3, 1, 4, 2.

questions.q: Which of the following words CANNOT be formed using the letters of the word EXAMINATION?
questions.solution:
EXAMINATION has: E, X, A×2, M, I×2, N×2, T, O×1.
MOTION needs O twice, but there is only one O.
NATION, ANIMATE and TAXI can all be formed.

questions.q:
Arrange the following words in the order in which they appear in an English dictionary.
1. Peculiar 2. Pebble 3. Pedestal 4. Peck 5. Pedal
questions.solution:
All start with "Pe". Third letters: Peculiar (c), Pebble (b), Pedestal (d), Peck (c), Pedal (d).
b: Pebble first.
c: Peck vs Peculiar → "Peck" (k) vs "Pecu" (u) → Peck, then Peculiar.
d: Pedal vs Pedestal → "Peda" vs "Pede" → Pedal, then Pedestal.
Order: 2, 4, 1, 5, 3.

questions.q:
Which word will come THIRD in the dictionary order?
Excel, Exact, Exceed, Exalt
questions.solution:
"Exa…" words come before "Exc…" words.
Exact vs Exalt: c before l → Exact, Exalt.
Exceed vs Excel: "Excee" vs "Excel" → e before l → Exceed, Excel.
Order: Exact, Exalt, Exceed, Excel. Third = Exceed.

questions.q: Which of the following words CANNOT be formed using the letters of the word CONSTITUTION?
questions.solution:
CONSTITUTION has: C, O×2, N×2, S, T×3, I×2, U.
CONSTANT needs the letter A, which is not present.
TUITION, NOTION and COUNTS can all be formed.

questions.q:
Which word will come FOURTH in the dictionary order?
Monitor, Money, Monarch, Monetary, Monastery
questions.solution:
All start with "Mon". Fourth letters: a (Monarch, Monastery), e (Money, Monetary), i (Monitor).
Monarch vs Monastery: r before s → Monarch, Monastery.
Monetary vs Money: "Monet" vs "Money" → t before y → Monetary, Money.
Order: Monarch, Monastery, Monetary, Money, Monitor. Fourth = Money.

flashcards.back: Compare letter by letter; at the first difference, the earlier alphabet letter wins.
Each letter can be used only as many times as it appears in the given word.
